question: In June 2025, a London-bound Air India aircraft crashed shortly after taking off from which airport?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ahmedabad Airport**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The specific aviation incident mentioned involves a **London-bound Air India aircraft** that crashed shortly after takeoff in **June 2025**.
 
• The flight originated from **Ahmedabad Airport**, formally known as **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport (SVPIA)**, which serves the state of **Gujarat**.
 
• **Air India**, the national carrier owned by the **Tata Group**, operates several direct international flights from **Ahmedabad** to major global hubs, including **London Heathrow** and **London Gatwick**.
 
• The crash occurred during the initial climb phase, a critical stage of flight shortly after leaving the runway at **Ahmedabad**.
 
• As per the question, the departure point was neither **Delhi**, **Chennai**, nor **Kolkata**, but specifically the international terminal at **Ahmedabad**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Ahmedabad Airport.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport (SVPIA):**
 
 
• Located in **Hansol**, it is the busiest airport in **Gujarat** and serves both **Ahmedabad** and the state capital, **Gandhinagar**.
 
• It features two main terminals: **Terminal 1** for domestic flights and **Terminal 2** for international operations.
 
• The airport is named after **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**, the first **Deputy Prime Minister** of India.
 
 
 
• **Air India International Operations:**
 
 
• **Air India** maintains a significant presence in the **United Kingdom** market due to the large **Gujarati diaspora** residing there.
 
• Direct connectivity between **Ahmedabad** and **London** is a high-demand route, often utilizing long-haul aircraft like the **Boeing 787 Dreamliner** or **Boeing 777**.
 
• Under the **Tata Group**'s ownership since **January 2022**, the airline has been undergoing a massive transformation project named **Vihaan.AI**.
 
 
 
• **Aviation Safety and Investigation:**
 
 
• In India, any major aircraft accident is investigated by the **Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB)**, which operates under the **Ministry of Civil Aviation**.
 
• The **Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA)** is the regulatory body that oversees safety standards and pilot licensing in the country.
 
• Takeoff and landing are statistically the most vulnerable phases of flight, accounting for a high percentage of aviation incidents globally.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Airport Codes:** The IATA code for **Ahmedabad Airport** is **AMD**, while the ICAO code is **VAAH**.
 
• **Geographical Significance:** The airport is situated approximately **9 kilometers** from the city center of **Ahmedabad**.
 
• **Historical Context:** Air India has a long history of flying to the **United Kingdom**, dating back to its first international flight to **London** in **June 1948**.
 
• **Emergency Protocols:** In the event of a crash shortly after takeoff, airports activate the **Airport Emergency Plan (AEP)**, involving the **Airport Fire Service** and local medical teams for immediate rescue operations.
